first.rationale:
The competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the emotionally obvious move, but memory_73 is the single inherited claim that carries an explicit methodological defect: the readout pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, so its 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' may be an artifact of the pooling rather than a real effect. Committing the only slot this week to a discount program on the strength of a known-compromised readout is exactly the failure mode to avoid, and discount-led acquisition is the direction most likely to buy short-term logos at the expense of sustainable qualified revenue. So I spend one verification pull on memory_73 to see whether the underlying record survives de-pooling.

The second pull goes to memory_86 because it is the load-bearing claim under my intended action and the closest match to the observed symptoms: onboarding completion is down 4% and activation is down 6% QoQ, which is precisely the funnel stage memory_86 and memory_31 describe. Two independent-looking memories (day 24 and day 52) both point at top-of-funnel friction, and memory_91 suggests activation messaging is complementary rather than competing. I want to confirm memory_86's effect was measured on completion and time-to-value rather than on a vanity step, and that it was not itself a pooled or redefined readout, before treating the convergence of memory_31 and memory_86 as real corroboration rather than two echoes of one original finding.

Intent: simplify_onboarding at standard experiment scale. It addresses the internally-caused decline we can actually control, it is reversible, and it does not structurally discount the revenue base. I am deliberately not treating promotional_pricing as ruled out — it is deferred pending what the archive says about memory_73. If verification shows memory_73's lift holds after separating the cohorts, pricing becomes a live candidate for the next slot; if it shows the lift was an artifact, that memory should be down-weighted so future sessions do not inherit it at face value. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) and referral_incentive (memory_57) look sound but target segments that are not where the current bleeding is. Residual uncertainty: I do not yet know whether the activation drop is upstream (onboarding friction) or independent, so the experiment should instrument activation separately rather than assuming onboarding gains propagate.
